papers.title: Surface Enhanced Anisotropy and Its Impacts on Massive Neutron Star Configurations in Einstein Gravity : Stability, Structure, and Multimessenger Consistency
papers.abstract: Anisotropic neutron-star configurations are investigated within Einstein's General Relativity using a third-order polynomial equation of state, (p_r=A\rho+B\rho^2+C\rho^3), and the Buchdahl class-I metric ansatz, (e^{q(r)}=\frac{L(1+\tau r^2)}{L-\tau r^2}). Physically viable interior solutions are constructed and smoothly matched to the exterior Schwarzschild spacetime using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The stellar properties are examined through the matter distribution, pressure anisotropy, hydrostatic equilibrium, compactness, surface redshift, tidal deformability, causality, and dynamical stability. The energy density and radial and tangential pressures remain finite, positive, and monotonically decreasing throughout the interior, while the anisotropy vanishes at the centre and increases smoothly toward the surface. Generalized Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation confirms equilibrium through the balance of gravitational, hydrostatic, and anisotropic forces. Furthermore, adiabatic index satisfies the Chandrasekhar stability criterion, and both sound speeds obey the causality and Herrera cracking conditions. The compactness remains below the Buchdahl limit, with physically acceptable surface redshifts. The predicted maximum masses exceed the corresponding observed masses, with some configurations extending into the lower mass-gap region. The tidal deformabilities are consistent with multimessenger constraints from GW170817 and NICER. In addition, the theoretical mass-compactness relation and its prediction intervals show good agreement with observational estimates. Finally, Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis provides statistically reliable constraints on the tidal Love number, compactness, and perturbation parameter. These results establish a physically viable and observationally compatible framework for describing anisotropic neutron stars within General Relativity.

papers.title: Periodic orbits and gravitational wave radiation of a phantom Dirac--Born--Infeld regular black hole Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate periodic orbits and gravitational wave radiation in the spacetime of an asymptotically flat regular black hole supported by a phantom Dirac--Born--Infeld scalar field. Starting from the timelike geodesic equations, we examine the effective potential and the characteristic circular orbits and construct periodic zoom--whirl trajectories. We further explore the sensitivity of orbital closure to small energy perturbations and examine the periastron advance of the $S2$ star around Sgr A$^*$ to assess possible constraints on the regular core parameter. The gravitational wave signals associated with representative periodic trajectories are then calculated within a quadrupole based numerical kludge approximation, considering both polarization modes. Particular attention is given to the influence of the regular core on orbital configurations and waveform characteristics, providing a complementary perspective on gravitational aspects of phantom Dirac--Born--Infeld regular black holes.

papers.title: Observational signatures of Bardeen black holes under nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the shadow and optical appearance of the Bardeen black hole (BH) within nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED). Since photon propagation in nonlinear electromagnetic field can be equivalently described as null-geodesic motion in the effective metric induced by NLED, we derive the corresponding effective optical geometry of the NLED-Bardeen BH. Furthermore, by examining the horizon-photon sphere-shadow inequality, we demonstrate that the NLED-Bardeen BH does not satisfy the complete inequality chain. In addition, we investigate photon dynamics and the corresponding optical images generated by both thin disk and spherical accretion models. Increasing $g/M$ reduces the photon sphere radius and critical impact parameter, resulting in a more compact shadow and an inward shift of the emission peak. For the thin disk accretion model, photon trajectories are classified into direct emission, lensing ring, and photon ring components according to the corresponding impact parameter. We find that Model 1 exhibits three distinct intensity peaks, whereas Models 2 and 3 display two and one peaks. The systematic dependence of these features on the magnetic charge indicates that the NLED-Bardeen BH may exhibit observational signatures distinguishable from those of the Bardeen BH. In static spherical accretion, the intensity peaks near the critical impact parameter because of the enhanced optical path length, while infalling spherical accretion introduces an additional Doppler redshift that suppresses the observed intensity. These results indicate that the shadow size, ring structure, and intensity distribution can serve as potential observational signatures of NLED effects in the strong-field regime.

papers.title: Analogue Gravity: the Subcritical Case
papers.abstract: We focus on the subcritical case in Analogue Gravity for a subluminal dispersion relation, and investigate the problem of pair creation in the absence of an horizon analytically, for the subcritical white hole case. We limit our attention to weakly dispersive media. In particular, we take into account for simplicity the Corley model and adopt an approach inspired by quantum mechanics in the so-called overbarrier scattering. The presence of complex turning points is shown to play a fundamental role in allowing a mode conversion which would be absent in a naive WKB approach. We show that there is still a pair creation phenomenon, which, in the subcritical case, is non-Planckian and without a Hawking partner. Our fully analytical results are qualitatively in agreement with the literature at hand. Furthermore we confirm the existence of a critical regime betwen the subcritical and the transcritical ones where no pair creation occurs.

papers.title: Optimal summary statistics to constrain w0waCDM with the DESI BGS
papers.abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is the first stage-4 spectroscopic instrument installed on the 4-m Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona. It contains 5000 robotically positioned fibers, allowing the measurement of as many galaxy spectra in one observation (~20 minutes). The data acquisition (2021--2028) aims at constraining the cosmological parameters, and especially the parameters describing the evolution of the dark energy with time. However, standard clustering analysis based on 2-point statistics only capture the Gaussian information of the matter density field, while the analytical models used to match these statistical probe are limited to quasi-linear scales, as they are based on perturbation theory. Therefore, the non-Gaussian and non-linear information of the density field is not exploited. To go beyond these limitations, several alternative clustering methods have been developed that rely on a simulation-based pipeline. In this presentation, we focus on the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey, a magnitude-limited sample of bright galaxies in the redshift range of 0.1 < z < 0.4. We present how accessing the non-linear and non-Gaussian information of the density field allows around 40% improvement on the constraints of some $\Lambda$CDM parameters. We are also extending the method to constrain w0waCDM in order to improve DESI's sensibility at low redshift where the Universe is dominated by dark energy.

papers.title: Gravitational Production of Non-minimally Coupled Vector Dark Matter in Warm Inflation
papers.abstract: We study the purely gravitational production of a massive vector dark matter with a non-minimal coupling to the Einstein tensor, $\xi G_{\mu\nu}X^\mu X^\nu$, in warm inflation. The background, $V=\lambda\phi^4$ with a dissipation coefficient linear in temperature, is constrained by CMB observations and parametrized by the dissipation ratio $10^{-4}\le Q_0\le1$. We consider both unavoidable production channels: freeze-in from the Standard Model bath through graviton exchange, and cosmological gravitational particle production (CGPP). For freeze-in, we compute the scattering amplitudes including the contact interaction induced by $\xi$, which enhances the production of light dark matter through the longitudinal mode and suppresses that of heavy dark matter through destructive interference. For CGPP, the slow-roll parameter is not small during warm inflation, which enhances the production of light dark matter by up to three orders of magnitude relative to cold inflation. Combining both channels, CGPP excludes most of the light freeze-in branch, leaving $m_X\lesssim2.4\times10^{-5}$ GeV, a narrow window around $10^{10}$ GeV for strong dissipation, and $m_X\gtrsim10^{14}$--$10^{15}$ GeV. Only the heavy branch remains viable for all $|\xi|\lesssim1$.

papers.title: First detection of the forbidden rotational spectrum of H$_3^+$: JWST/MIRI observations of the shocked gas in HH 168
papers.abstract: The H$_3^+$ molecular ion is the cornerstone of interstellar ion-molecule chemistry. Its vibrational transitions have long been observed, in absorption along many interstellar sight lines and in emission from the upper atmospheres of the giant planets, but its pure rotational spectrum, which consists only of "forbidden" transitions made possible by centrifugal distortion, had not been observed in the laboratory or in any astronomical source. With JWST/MIRI we have detected this spectrum toward the Herbig-Haro object HH 168 in Cepheus A West. Twenty-six lines are detected above 5 $\sigma$ in one or both of two fields, of which the (J,K) = (5,0) -> (4,3) line at 16.325 $\mu$m is the strongest. The H$_3^+$ lines share the velocity and spatial distribution of the hot shocked H$_2$, not of the ionized gas. A rotation diagram yields a rotational temperature of ~ 730 K, but the level populations are not thermal and are best explained by subthermal excitation in gas at > 2000 K. We compare the observations with models of shocks propagating into mildly irradiated molecular gas. Constrained by the H$_2$ rotational lines, a dissociative J-type shock predicts H$_3^+$ emission within a factor ~1.5 of that observed, while a nondissociative C-type shock, which fits the H$_2$ lines better, underpredicts it by a factor 5-6, although the excitation of H$_3^+$ by energetic collisions is poorly known. Archival MIRI data show the H$_3^+$ forbidden rotational spectrum in the HH 211 bow shock. The H$_3^+$ lines provide a new probe of the ionization in shocked molecular gas.

papers.title: First detection of suprathermal CH$^+$ rotational emissions from chemical pumping: JWST/MIRI observations of the HH 168 molecular shock
papers.abstract: The methylidyne cation forms in warm or shocked interstellar gas through the endothermic reaction C$^+$ + H$_2$ -> CH$^+$ + H. Because C$^+$, which is common in irradiated and shocked gas, reacts with H$_2$ only when the reactants supply > 0.4 eV, CH$^+$ traces energy deposition in molecular gas. JWST/MIRI observations of HH 168 reveal the pure rotational lines R(17)-R(31) of CH$^+$ at 13.7-21.3 micron, from upper levels J = 18-32 (0.57-1.65 eV). Eleven lines exceed 5 sigma in both of the two fields that we observed and match the hot H$_2$ in radial velocity and spatial distribution. Because collisional excitation is negligible, each ion entering the v = 0 ladder emits one photon in every R(J) line below its entry level, so the line intensities provide the first measured rotational distribution of the ground-state products. The photon intensity falls almost linearly with increasing J, as expected for formation at a similar rate into every level up to J ~ 33; formation in J = 32 requires > 2 eV of reactant energy. The line positions, up to 150 km/s redward of ExoMol predictions, provide the first measurement of the CH$^+$ rotational intervals above J = 16. A Boltzmann distribution at $\phi T$ ~ 6200 K, where $\phi$ is the fraction of the available energy appearing in rotation, fits slightly better, implying reactant energies equivalent to several thousand kelvin. These lines probe the dynamics of a prototypical interstellar ion-molecule reaction.

papers.title: A DOLPHOT/Euclid Study of the Resolved, Faint Outer Milky Way Globular Cluster AM-1
papers.abstract: We present a resolved star study of AM-1, a distant ($D \simeq 120$ kpc), faint ($M_V \sim -5.1$) Milky Way (MW) globular cluster, based on Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) imaging. To perform photometry of the Euclid VIS and NISP imaging, we develop a Euclid-specific module for the crowded field stellar photometry package DOLPHOT. We construct and present empirical point spread function (PSF) models for VIS and NISP, along with a photometric calibration, entirely from the public Q1 images. Our photometry reaches $5\sigma$ point source depths of $I_E, Y_E, J_E, H_E = 27.1, 25.3, 25.5, 25.3$, $\sim$1-1.5 mag deeper than the public Q1 catalog, as expected for dedicated resolved star PSF photometry. We resolve the cluster to $\sim$1 mag below its main sequence turnoff in all bands. The Euclid photometry agrees with color-magnitude diagram (CMD) modeling of archival HST/WFPC2 imaging and with the 2MASS-anchored VISTA Hemisphere Survey to $\lesssim0.02$ mag in $I_E$, $J_E$, and $H_E$, with a $\sim$0.07 mag offset in $Y_E$. We find that AM-1 hosts an old ($\sim$10.6 Gyr), intermediate-metallicity ([Fe/H] $\sim -1$) population, with a present-day stellar mass of $\sim 2\times10^4\,M_\odot$ and $M/L_V \simeq 2.2$, and has a half-light radius of $\sim$12-16 pc with a round, low-concentration profile. These affirm earlier studies placing AM-1 among the most extended, diffuse outer-halo clusters, which dynamical work identifies as accreted. We describe and publicly release DOLPHOT v2.1, the Euclid module, and its empirical PSFs, which together enable Euclid resolved star studies ranging from faint MW systems such as AM-1 to more luminous galaxies throughout the Local Volume. We anticipate further refinements, including spatially varying PSFs, with Euclid Data Release 1.

papers.title: Classical Cepheids in the 4MOST era I: Methodology for 4MOST variable stars and NLTE abundance gradients in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: Classical Cepheids (CCs) are key distance indicators and tracers of young stellar populations in the Milky Way. Their period-luminosity-metallicity (PLZ) relation also makes them calibrators of the Hubble constant $H_0$. Despite their importance, chemical composition, especially non-LTE (NLTE) effects, remains a significant source of systematics in PLZ applications. In preparation for the large CCs sample expected from the 4MIDABLE-HR (4MOST Consortium Survey 4: Milky Way Disc and Bulge High-Resolution) survey, we present a method for deriving Cepheid atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances in NLTE. Using the Payne artificial neural network (ANN) trained on NLTE spectra, we derive atmospheric parameters and abundances for 17 elements: O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Sr, Y, Ba, Eu in NLTE and C and Cr in LTE. We apply the new method to archival spectra of Cepheids and derive radial chemical gradients in the Milky Way. We derive robust NLTE stellar parameters and abundances for Cepheids spanning metallicities from $\sim -0.87$ to $\sim +0.35$ dex. For stars with multi-epoch spectra, we find that NLTE abundances are consistent across the pulsation cycle, whereas LTE values show larger dispersions and biases. The resulting abundance distributions and gradients align well with Galactic disk expectations from chemical evolution models. We confirm that the gradients flatten in the outer disk beyond $R_{\rm GC} \sim 15\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and provide the first NLTE gradients for Co, Ni, Y, and Eu. We show that our NLTE astrophysical analysis yields robust solutions for atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances across spectra at the resolving power of 4MOST-HR. This enables large, homogeneous studies with upcoming surveys such as 4MOST 4MIDABLE-HR and provides a solid basis for tightening constraints on Galactic chemical evolution models and Cepheid distance-scale work.

papers.title: Scalable early warning for binary neutron-star mergers in third-generation gravitational-wave detectors
papers.abstract: Third-generation gravitational-wave observatories will observe binary neutron-star coalescences for hours before merger. Over these extended time windows, Earth's motion and the long signal durations make standard search methods computationally demanding for low-latency detection. We propose an approach based on short-time Fourier transforms and convolutional neural networks that implicitly marginalizes over extrinsic parameters, effectively reducing the search to the chirp mass. The network learns the signals' nonlinear time-frequency morphology, approximating the optimal Bayesian detection statistic. Using a large-scale campaign of simulated signal injections, we compare the network's performance with a GPU-optimized matched-filtering baseline for both the ET$\Delta$ and ET2L configurations of the Einstein Telescope and signal durations from approximately 25 minutes ($f_{\rm min} = 5$ Hz) to approximately 6 hours ($f_{\rm min} = 2$ Hz). The network achieves comparable detection sensitivity while reducing computational costs by over four orders of magnitude, bringing processing times from minutes to milliseconds. This efficiency paves the way for rapid early-warning alerts for multi-messenger astronomy in the third-generation detector era.

papers.title: The impact of MUSE sky subtraction on unresolved stellar population end products: Study cases of NGC 1097 and NGC 1433
papers.abstract: One of the main steps in data reduction for ground-based astronomy is sky subtraction. For extended objects, it is necessary to observe dedicated sky frames, usually with airmass values similar to the target's, using different pointing strategies. However, it is not well documented how different observing strategies can affect the science end product. In particular, with the use of the MUSE/VLT, this can yield distinct stellar population products, such as age, metallicity, and \alpha-enhancement. To address this, we considered two case studies seeking to investigate: (i) the sky stability in observations taken consecutively over a period of 2 hours with thin sky transparency and airmass values of 1.25-1.05, and (ii) the impact of different sky conditions on the same target. Among our main results, we find that for galaxies with 0.0014 < z < 0.0077, the sky line [NI] at \lambda 5200 coincides with the Mgb bandpass, which is essential for metallicity measurements, highlighting the need for proper sky subtraction. In addition, for regions with relative fluxes above 10 with respect to the sky in NGC1097, sky frames with variation up to ~18 % still retrieve consistent stellar population properties - in this case, this corresponds to flux values of >1500 x 10^-20 erg/s/cm^2 and Johnson-V ~19.0. In contrast, when comparing data from different nights for NGC1433, fainter regions suffer greatly from distinct sky conditions, especially in metallicity measurements, which range within +/- 0.2, strongly affecting the interpretation of stellar mass assembly and the origin of the gas (i.e., mergers might bring metal-poor gas, while an in-situ burst of star formation can yield metal-rich stars). This study is the first of its kind and highlights the importance of proper sky subtraction, providing insights regarding data limitations and observational strategies for future observations with MUSE.

papers.title: Local Pitch Angles of Galactic Structures in Nearby Galaxies with JWST: I. Spiral Arms and Interarm Substructures in Disk-Dominated Systems
papers.abstract: We present a spatially resolved study of spiral arms and feather substructures in seven nearby galaxies observed with JWST. Using eight images per galaxy, from four NIRCam and four MIRI filters, we combine a two-dimensional Fourier transform (2D-FT) with a circular-window correlation method to measure both global and local pitch angles. The 2D-FT identifies the dominant azimuthal mode and the corresponding $p_{\rm max}$, allowing us to reconstruct the spiral pattern and define arm and interarm masks. We then apply cosine filters with different pitch angles and window sizes in the $(\ln (R),\theta)$ plane to map the pitch-angle distribution across multiple spatial scales. NIRCam images provide the most robust measurements of the main spiral pattern, whereas MIRI data reveal dusty interarm features, particularly feathers, with greater contrast at the smallest window size ($D_w=0.25$). Across the sample, the main arms typically have $|\alpha|\simeq15^\circ$--$30^\circ$, while feathers show systematically larger values, often above $50^\circ$. These results demonstrate that pitch angle is scale dependent and that different structural components within the same galaxy can occupy distinct angular regimes. NIRCam and MIRI therefore offer complementary views of spiral structure, with the former tracing the large-scale stellar backbone and the latter exposing finer dust substructures. Together with the companion study of barred galaxies, this work provides a common framework for using local pitch angles to investigate distinct dynamical environments in nearby galaxies.

papers.title: Local Pitch Angles of Galactic Structures in Nearby Galaxies with JWST: II. Dust Lanes and Gas Flows in Bar-Dominated Systems
papers.abstract: We present a spatially resolved study of local pitch angles in six barred spiral galaxies observed by PHANGS--JWST, focusing on bar-dominated regions where dust lanes are the main structures. We combine a two-dimensional Fourier transform (2D-FT) with a circular-window correlation method to map pitch angles across multiple wavelengths and spatial scales, extending our previous analysis of spiral arms and interarm substructures in disk-dominated galaxies. The dust lanes show relatively large pitch angles, typically $|\alpha|\simeq35^\circ$--$70^\circ$, well above those measured for spiral arms. In several galaxies, the pitch angle changes systematically along the dust lane, with smaller values in the inner regions and larger values farther along the bar, tracing variations in local curvature. The multi-scale analysis shows that larger windows recover the overall geometry of the dust lanes, whereas smaller windows reveal local irregularities and secondary structures. MIRI images generally provide the clearest view of the dust morphology and allow a more precise characterization of local pitch-angle variations, while NIRCam offers a complementary view of the underlying stellar distribution. Unlike spiral-arm pitch angles, which are commonly associated with density-wave patterns, the values measured here characterize the local orientation and curvature of dust lanes associated with bar-driven gas flows. Together with the results of our companion study of disk-dominated galaxies, these findings support a unified, scale-dependent framework in which local pitch angles serve as observational diagnostics of distinct dynamical regimes in nearby galaxies.

papers.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition
papers.abstract: Weak gravitational lensing is a powerful cosmological probe that enables direct mapping of the matter distribution and precise constraints on the fundamental parameters governing structure formation in the universe. In recent years, machine learning has shown strong potential for extracting cosmological information from weak-lensing data beyond traditional summary statistics. However, progress has been limited by the lack of standardized benchmarks that capture the complexity of the dataset, simulator imperfections, and various systematic biases encountered in realistic analyses. To address this gap, we present the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge, one of the NeurIPS 2025 competitions, as a benchmark dataset and evaluation study. Our dataset reflects realistic weak-lensing observations, incorporating multiple systematic biases, and thereby providing a controlled testbed for robust cosmological inference under uncertainties. We summarize the main methodological advances developed by the winners of our challenge, including data augmentation with conditional optimal transport, an AI-agent-driven approach for parameter inference, ensemble learning, Vision Transformer-based architectures, and physics-informed feature integration. By unifying the benchmark dataset and the winning solutions, this work provides a community resource for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for weak lensing cosmology and, more broadly, for scientific inference under systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Stealth scalars on prescribed dark-energy backgrounds: reconstruction, branch regularity, and perturbative bounds
papers.abstract: We reconstruct homogeneous stealth scalar fields on prescribed Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker backgrounds with constant or evolving dark-energy equations of state. The scalar stress tensor vanishes, so the expansion history is supported by an independent background sector. Eliminating the self-interaction potential yields a Riccati equation for the scalar profile. We use it to distinguish exact stealthness from global regularity and from the stronger identification of a term in the scalar stress tensor with the prescribed dark-energy density. We prove that this sector-preserving identification is not dynamically invariant in a mixed flat constant-$w$ cosmology. For radiation-free $w$CDM backgrounds, a hypergeometric representation allows the regular and singular branches to be separated by a background-dependent threshold. At conformal coupling the reconstruction instead reduces to an exact comoving-distance quadrature, valid for arbitrary regular flat histories, including radiation. A CPL phantom-divide crossing does not singularize the background stealth equation, although the perturbations of the prescribed dark-energy sector require an independent treatment. The scalar--tensor description gives luminal high-frequency propagation under a positive effective Planck mass. If the field tracks its cosmological value locally without screening, Cassini constraints strongly suppress the corresponding late-time gravitational responses.

papers.title: Relativistic Simulations of Self-Gravitating Radiation Fluids
papers.abstract: We present an approach for numerical simulations of pure radiation fluids within the general relativistic hydrodynamics framework. The approach models radiation as a self-gravitating perfect fluid with vanishing rest mass, enabling simulations of radiation fluids in strong-gravity spacetimes. Building on the existing relativistic hydrodynamics code Whisky, within the Einstein Toolkit framework, we introduce modifications to incorporate radiation fluids, including updates to the source terms, recovery scheme, and Riemann solvers. Modifications are validated using standard shock tube tests. We present results for radiation accretion onto a single black hole, as well as a photon star solution for radiation in unstable hydrostatic equilibrium, demonstrating both collapse and dispersion under perturbations.

papers.title: Time-Delay Recovery in AGN Reverberation Mapping via Mutual Information
papers.abstract: Active galactic nuclei exhibit complex, nonlinear multiwavelength variability that standard cross-correlation techniques, sensitive only to linear covariance, may fail to capture fully. We apply time-lagged Mutual Information (MI) lag estimation, via the Kraskov-Stoegbauer-Grassberger $k$-nearest-neighbour estimator ($k = 5$) with a 150-iteration Random Subset Selection bootstrap, to the light curves of four Seyfert galaxies (Mrk 509, NGC 5548, NGC 4151, and NGC 4593) monitored across eight energy bands by Swift. In the UV/optical regime the MI estimator successfully reproduces the inter-band disc reprocessing lags established by the interpolated cross-correlation function, with performance degrading toward the optical where low variability amplitude produces poorly defined MI peaks. In the X-ray bands, where the physical X-ray/UV coupling is known to be weak, the estimator fails to recover consistent lags across the sample, with the notable exception of NGC 4593. Contextualising these outcomes within the multifractal characterisation of our previous work, we discuss how MI performance relates to the multifractal spectral width $\Delta\alpha$ of each band, and we propose $\Delta\alpha$ as a candidate diagnostic for anticipating where MI-based reverberation mapping is likely to succeed or fail in multiband datasets of active galactic nuclei.

papers.title: HINSPHERES: Spherically Symmetric Radiative Transfer Modeling of HINSA and the Radial HI-to-H$_2$ Transition in Molecular Clouds
papers.abstract: The transition from atomic hydrogen (HI) to molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) is the first step in the evolution from diffuse interstellar gas to dense star-forming cores. HI narrow self-absorption (HINSA), produced by cold atomic gas mixed with molecular material, provides a direct tracer of the HI-to-H$_2$ transition in molecular clouds. Existing HINSA analyses typically model HINSA as a single Gaussian component with a uniform spin temperature. This approach cannot recover the radial HI distribution and yields large errors for young cores whose profiles deviate from a Gaussian shape. Here we present hinspheres, an open-source framework that models the core as onion-like spherically symmetric concentric shells, solves radiative transfer along the line of sight and jointly fits the HI abundance, temperature, and kinematic parameters. The framework recovers all parameters with a mean relative error of 4.6-6.8% on our synthetic data with different ages. A combined resolution-noise grid shows that the median recovery error remains below 16% for cores within 1 kpc observed at FAST resolution with noise levels below 0.2 K. Applying it to the dark cores L1574 and L1544, we reveal radial HI abundance profiles that span about three orders of magnitude, which were missed by the single-Gaussian method. The derived chemical ages are $6.5\times10^6$ and $8.7\times10^6$ yr, respectively. papers.title: B-fields In STar-forming Region Observations (BISTRO): Population-Level Universality and Environmental Structuring of 450/850 $μ$m Polarization Signatures

Across 35 regions with reliable spectral indices of total ($\alpha$) and polarized ($\gamma$) intensity, the medians over sources are $\langle\alpha\rangle = 3.33$ and $\langle\gamma\rangle = 2.85$-$3.04$. The median $\gamma - \alpha$ is $-0.57$ to $-0.45$, with $\gamma < \alpha$ in 24-27 regions. These ranges span the two extreme placements of $3\sigma$ limits for polarized intensity below the noise floor. The position angles at the two wavelengths agree within $10^\circ$ in 10 of 13 regional medians, disfavoring a geometric origin that would rotate the angles. The medians of $\gamma-\alpha$ in 9 low-mass, 19 high-mass and 7 Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) regions are not ordered low-mass $<$ high-mass $<$ CMZ (Jonckheere-Terpstra $p = 0.43$-$0.70$). A difference among classes is not robustly detected. The Kruskal-Wallis $p = 0.056$-$0.078$ becomes $p = 0.026$-$0.041$ when the Rosette Molecular Cloud alone is excluded, although the high-mass class has the lowest median in every treatment. The classes follow a distance sequence (the beam spans 0.008-0.51 pc), coupling environment and physical scale. Within clouds, the 450 $\mu$m polarization fraction decreases with Herschel column density in all 7 fields with sufficient dynamic range. Coefficients from pooled pixels mix trends within clouds, differences between clouds, and the influence of OMC 1. They therefore do not define a single law for individual pixels. The wavelength dependence across sources provides a benchmark for grain alignment. We cannot order it by environment and do not propose a unique mechanism.

papers.title: Shallow-water black holes and lattice superradiance
papers.abstract: Rotating black holes can amplify waves that scatter off them, a process known as superradiance that fluid analogues bring into the laboratory. Separating the horizon's role from dissipation in the surrounding fluid remains difficult. Here we realise a rotating analogue black hole in a lattice fluid: a shallow-water vortex whose horizon is set by a topographic sill, so that the only sink lies behind a supercritical layer that lets nothing out. We measure superradiance as energy extraction: the flux at the horizon is outward for co-rotating waves whose pattern rotates more slowly than the horizon, and inward for faster waves, counter-rotating waves and a non-rotating hole. A scan over three lattice viscosities separates the extraction at the horizon, which is inviscid, from that of the viscous fluid inside the corotation radius: well below the band edge the horizon is the absorber; near the edge the viscous share is half at the operating viscosity and vanishes at the lowest. A drain-anchored horizon, as in water-tank experiments, gives the same signs. Our analysis gives insight into the mechanism of superradiance and offers a cheap, flexible platform for designing analogue-gravity experiments.

papers.title: Engineering a digital acoustic black hole
papers.abstract: We show how to design and build an analogue black hole as a synchronous digital circuit. We define the sound speed, the flow and the horizon of such a circuit in terms of its own logic, and realise one on a field-programmable gate array, where the black hole is probed electrically with a signal generator and an oscilloscope. We measure the stability of the horizon, its causal cone, the ringdown and rotational superradiance. A single flipped bit inside the horizon leaks out by an amount that falls exponentially with depth. Digital circuits thus form a reconfigurable class of gravitational analogues and realise an analogue black hole as a cellular automaton.

papers.title: The hierarchical structure of the Milky Way I. A model-agnostic clustering of 1 billion stars in 5D
papers.abstract: The Milky Way exhibits a hierarchical structure shaped by mergers, accretion, and internal dynamics. Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) enables a global view of this structure, but requires scalable, model-agnostic methods to extract multi-scale clustering patterns. We aim to characterise the hierarchical clustering structure of the Milky Way in a model-agnostic way and to assess how the resulting structures relate to existing catalogues. We apply the hierarchical density-based clustering algorithm AstroLink to a locally magnitude-complete subsample of over one billion Gaia DR3 stars with five-dimensional astrometric information. The data are corrected for selection effects and transformed using a distance contraction and feature scaling. We compare the resulting cluster hierarchy to catalogues of open clusters, globular clusters, dwarf galaxies, and stellar streams using custom availability-aware metrics and a bi-directional best-match framework. At a significance threshold of $S = 3.8\sigma$, AstroLink identifies 7410 statistically significant clusters spanning a wide range of morphologies. Compact systems are often recovered as reciprocal matches with many also exhibiting internal substructure, while extended structures are typically fragmented or partially recovered. A substantial fraction of clusters have no counterpart in the comparison catalogues, these may be new structures but additional physical checks are needed to verify this. A model-agnostic, hierarchical clustering approach can recover the multi-scale structure of the Milky Way at Gaia DR3 scale and provides a unified framework for comparing heterogeneous catalogues and identifying candidate structures.

papers.title: ERG, axions, and a PT-symmetric accelerating Universe
papers.abstract: In conventional quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian is required to be Hermitian, ensuring real energy eigenvalues. Certain non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also possess entirely real spectra when they are invariant under the combined action of parity ($\mathcal P$) and time reversal ($\mathcal T$). Such Hamiltonians are called unbroken parity--time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric. We conjecture that, in a string-inspired scenario, a repulsive phase of gravity may be due to a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric gravitational theory, characterised by anomalous Chern-Simons terms, coupled to axion fields. The conjecture is based on the behaviour of the chiral anomalous couplings of these axions to electromagnetic potentials. Within the Exact Renormalisation Group (ERG) framework in the modified local potential approximation, we argue that singularities in the ERG beta functions for such couplings may indicate an infrared phase transition. At the energy scales of these singularities, we conjecture that the field theory transitions from the Hermitian phase to a ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal T}$-- symmetric theory, of gravity, characterised by a repulsive Netwon's ``constant''. This may induce the acceleration observed in the Universe at late eras, without the need for a dark--energy component.

papers.title: Constraining Cosmic Deceleration using the Solar System
papers.abstract: We investigate whether Solar System dynamics can provide independent constraints on the present day cosmological deceleration parameter $q_0$, offering a complementary approach to conventional cosmological probes. By relating cosmic acceleration to a weak Hooke type radial perturbation, we derive bounds using planetary perihelion precession, trans-Neptunian objects, and Oort cloud dynamics. We obtain relatively robust planetary bounds of $|q_0|\lesssim 10^9$, while the outer Solar System yields potentially stronger, albeit more model dependent, constraints approaching $10^5$. Through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analyses, we explore the statistical robustness of these estimates and their dependence on orbital measurements. Finally, we demonstrate how future precision astrometry and outer planet missions could improve these limits by several orders of magnitude, establishing Solar System dynamics as a complementary laboratory for probing cosmological acceleration.

papers.title: Generalized Second Law of Thermodynamics in $f(Q)$ Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the validity of the generalized second law (GSL) of thermodynamics on the cosmological apparent horizon in $f(Q)$ symmetric teleparallel gravity, using the Wald-type entropy prefactor $Af_Q/4G$ together with a correction term derived directly from the modified Friedmann equations. We derive, and verify by explicit symbolic computation, a closed-form expression for the apparent horizon entropy in $f(Q)$ gravity and show that its time derivative combines with the matter entropy rate into a remarkably compact master formula, $T_A\dot S_{\rm tot} = 4\pi\dot H(\dot H f_Q + H\dot f_Q)/H^4$ (in units $8\pi G=1$), which correctly reduces to the known general-relativistic limit. We apply this formalism to three observationally viable $f(Q)$ models --- power-law, exponential, and logarithmic. We find that the GSL is satisfied throughout cosmic history for all three models, and relate this robustness to a general, theory-independent structural condition: for ordinary pressureless matter obeying the null energy condition, GSL validity reduces to the sign of $\dot H$, i.e., to the absence of a phantom crossing in the total effective expansion history. The geometric sector exhibits model-dependent energy conditions, power-law and exponential models violate only the strong condition, while the logarithmic model violates the null, weak, and dominant conditions for \(z>-1\), and the strong condition for \(z<3.84\).

papers.title: Scalar-tensor reconstruction of coherent quantum black holes
papers.abstract: We construct a scalar-tensor realisation of spherically symmetric black hole geometries that effectively arise from quantum coherent states characterised by a finite core and finite extension. We determine the non-minimal coupling to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, kinetic coupling, and scalar potential and show that the kinetic term is positive only in finite domains. For fixed black hole mass, the boundaries of these domains provide a natural mechanism that relates the core size and spatial extension to the dynamics of the scalar-tensor realisation. We further show that the same geometry can also be obtained from a Horndeski action with derivative coupling and determine its domain of validity. Neither reconstruction includes the event horizon nor can it simultaneously reproduce arbitrarily large portions of the interior and exterior of the black hole, whose quantum origin therefore appears to remain partially outside the regime of applicability of semiclassical theories of gravity.

papers.title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
papers.abstract: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

papers.title: The Energy-Momentum Tensor of a Compact Object in General Relativity to all Multipole Orders
papers.abstract: In effective field theory approaches to compact object motion in general relativity, spin and tidal effects are encoded by operators formed from the Riemann tensor and its derivatives. Many such operators contribute degenerately to observables, with a single one often affecting several multipole moments of the body. We find the novel exact distributional formula for the energy-momentum tensor of a compact object in terms of its reduced multipole moments and these tensors.

papers.title: Variational Approach to the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon Equations of Motion for Extended Objects in General Relativity

papers.title: Studying the Fullerene Nest: JWST Observations of the Planetary Nebula Tc 1. II. A Spectroscopic and Spatial Study of C$_{60}$ and C$_{70}$ Emission
papers.abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the fullerene emission bands in JWST MIRI/MRS observations of the planetary nebula Tc 1. The observations reveal the emission features due to neutral C$_{60}$ and C$_{70}$ in unprecedented detail. The combined fullerene emission represents $\sim$2.6% of the total infrared output, suggesting that $\sim$0.6% of the carbon budget is locked up in fullerenes. We find no clear evidence for C$_{60}^+$, C$_{70}^+$ or C$_{60}^-$ in the spectrum. The high spectral resolution allows us to separate the fullerene bands from atomic emission lines for the first time, allowing for a much better characterization of the band profiles and yielding more accurate band ratios than previous observations. We see no spatial variation in the individual C$_{60}$ and C$_{70}$ band profile shapes across all pixels. The 17.4 and 18.9 $\mu$m C$_{60}$ bands show clear resolved ro-vibrational structure in their profiles, and similar structured emission is seen in the 12.5, 14.8, 17.7, and 21.8 $\mu$m C$_{70}$ bands, further establishing that all emitting fullerene molecules are in the gas phase. We report a higher 7.0/18.9 $\mu$m C$_{60}$ band ratio ($\sim$1.4-1.9) than previously reported ($\sim$1.3). We note that all bands, except the 8.5 $\mu$m band, contain a significant contribution from C$_{70}$, complicating the analysis. The fullerene emission is spatially concentrated in a thin, asymmetric shell at a radius of 5-6$''$ from the central star. The shell lies at the outer edge of the core of the nebula, which was ejected in a single, brief episode $\gtrsim$4,000 years ago.

papers.title: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
papers.abstract: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_\lambda$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(\Omega,g,k=\lambda g)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $\lambda$ below a geometrically determined threshold $\alpha$, while vanishing $E_\lambda$ at $\lambda=\alpha$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_\lambda=0$ when $\lambda=\alpha$, then $(\Omega,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/\lambda$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.

papers.title: Impact of the large scale environment on the baryonic scaling relations of disc galaxies: Insights from the GASP survey
papers.abstract: The Tully--Fisher relation (TFR) and the specific angular momentum--mass relation (SAMR) link the baryonic content of a disc to its kinematics and dynamics. Hence, these scaling relations should bear the imprints of any process removing baryons or altering their kinematics, such as those acting in clusters of galaxies. We test this using the MUSE survey "GAs Stripping Phenomena in galaxies" (GASP), which targets field, group, and cluster members at $z \approx 0.05$ and various stages of ram pressure stripping. For the 81 discs with favourable inclinations, we measure the distribution and kinematics of stars and ionised gas, and their specific angular momenta. Within their scatter, the stellar and baryonic relations show no significant dependence on the large scale environment: the TFRs have slopes $\alpha \approx 3.6$ and $\approx 3.5$ for any kinematic tracer, and the SAMRs have $\alpha \approx 0.65$--$0.75$, as predicted by tidal torque theory. The same holds for the ten S0-S0/as in our sample, consistent with the "faded spiral" formation scenario. Only the gas SAMR shows an environmental signature, with ram pressure stripped galaxies lying $\approx 0.16$~dex below unperturbed ones. This offset is mostly due to their enhanced star formation rate, and thus higher gas mass when inferred through the Schmidt-Kennicutt law, rather than to kinematic perturbations or disc truncation. Our results suggest that, within the area probed by MUSE ($\lesssim6$ disc scale lengths), these discs have preserved the angular momentum acquired at formation not only from cluster processes and pre-processing in filaments, but also from mergers and ejective feedback acting in any environment.

papers.title: Qubit representation of the mass observable in quantized Schwarzschild interior
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum-computational framework for the mass observable of the Wheeler--DeWitt quantized Schwarzschild black-hole interior. Working in the physical sector spanned by correlated two-mode oscillator states, we construct finite-dimensional representations of the mass operator and map them onto qubit operators through Pauli decomposition. We analyze the resulting representations for increasing truncation sizes and establish analytically the scaling of the number of nonvanishing Pauli terms and independent measurement settings. These results provide a quantitative characterization of the quantum resources required to encode and measure the black-hole mass observable. As a representative benchmark, we implement a two-qubit variational quantum eigensolver for the smallest nontrivial truncation and find excellent agreement with the exact finite-dimensional spectrum. We further describe a quantum-circuit procedure for verifying the Wheeler--DeWitt constraint independently of the mass estimation. Our results provide a direct connection between Wheeler--DeWitt quantum gravity and quantum computation and establish a structured route toward the quantum simulation of gravitational observables.

papers.abstract: We study a four-dimensional charged Letelier--anti-de Sitter (AdS) black-hole metric containing a cloud of strings, a phenomenological perfect-fluid-dark-matter (PFDM) source, and a Kiselev-type quintessence term. A rectangular benchmark cycle gives $W=0.095000$ and $\eta\simeq15.39\%$ for the explicitly stated geometric-unit parameters; these values are model- and cycle-specific and are not presented as a universal efficiency enhancement. For geometric optics, we derive the photon-sphere condition, critical impact parameter, and finite-radius shadow angle. For a massless, minimally coupled scalar field, we obtain a radial-coordinate Helmholtz equation and identify frequency-dependent barriers, evanescent intervals, and candidate trapping regions; the eikonal barrier-top scale approaches the photon-sphere capture scale. Two qualifications delimit the interpretation. First, with the stated PFDM stress-tensor convention, $\rho_{\rm PFDM}=-\beta/(8\pi r^3)$, so positive $\beta$ describes a negative-density effective source. Second, the mass function follows from the horizon equation, but identifying it with a conserved asymptotic AdS mass requires a separate charge and boundary-normalization analysis. The potential-well analysis likewise does not determine complex quasinormal frequencies. We therefore present the results as a consistent, parameter-specific analysis of the adopted phenomenological geometry, while distinguishing algebraic thermodynamic identities from conclusions requiring asymptotic-charge or spectral calculations.

papers.title: Tidally-induced vertical asymmetries in the LMC bar and disk
papers.abstract: Past observations and simulations have shown that the bar in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) may be tilted with respect to the disk plane, and that the outer LMC disk could be warped. These studies propose that the tilted bar and the warp in the LMC are induced by the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) pericentric passages. We analyze and quantify the effect of the SMC passage on the vertical position and kinematic asymmetries of both the bar and disk, as a function of different impact parameters or initial conditions. We used seven representative simulations from the KRATOS suite of $N$-body simulations of the LMC, SMC and Milky Way (MW) system for this analysis. To classify bar particles and analyze the bar and disk separately, we adopted a classification method based on persistent homology. To quantify the vertical asymmetries in the bar and disk of the LMC-like galaxy, we applied Fourier decomposition. We constructed Gaia DR3 mock catalogs to study whether the observed vertical asymmetries in Gaia DR3 are caused by astrometric uncertainties. We detect strong $m = 1$ vertical asymmetries in the bar and disk of the LMC-like galaxy for all interacting simulations after the pericentric passage of the SMC-like galaxy, indicative of a warped bar and disk. We also detect $m=2$ vertical asymmetries in the bar of the LMC-like galaxy for some simulations, indicative of a buckling bar. We conclude that the SMC passages induce vertical asymmetries in both the bar and the disk of the LMC, compatible to those measured in Gaia DR3. Tidal interactions naturally give rise to a warped and buckling LMC bar, and a warped LMC disk. Comparison between our results and Gaia DR3 suggest that models with a higher mass ratio between the SMC and the LMC may be favorable for reproducing the observed tilt of the LMC bar, and that the most recent SMC pericentric passage occurred at most 210 to 300 Myr ago.

papers.title: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
papers.abstract: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-V\theta)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $\kappa/2\pi$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8\pi GT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-V\theta)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-V\theta$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.

Large late-lag leakage, reaching approximately 0.97 in the total set, identifies targets for additional driver measurements and richer temporal histories. The resulting seasonal map of individual, shared and joint influences complements the response delays and velocity structure measured by reverberation mapping, and provides specific causal hypotheses for the evolving broad-line region.

papers.title: Studying the Fullerene Nest: JWST Observations of the Planetary Nebula Tc 1. III. Tracing Fullerene-Linked Dust Variation

Spectral variations of the 9$\unicode{x2013}$13 $\mu$m plateau reveal at least three distinct components, peaking at 9.5 $\mu$m, 11 $\mu$m and 12 $\mu$m respectively. papers.title: Is Dark Energy Inhomogeneous?
papers.abstract: The discovery of dark matter deficient galaxies motivates a fundamental question: Could sufficiently large regions of the Universe be deficient in dark energy as well? We investigate this possibility by developing a phenomenological framework that distinguishes genuine dark energy deficiencies from ordinary matter voids through nonlinear expansion, coherent peculiar velocities and density-momentum correlations. We show that a $10\%$ dark energy deficiency can suppress the expansion of a representative nonlinear void by approximately $2.7\%$, generating peculiar velocity residuals of order $60$-$100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ across scales of $30$-$50\, Mpc$. Intriguingly, we find that deficiencies of order $20\%$ extending over several hundred megaparsecs could also influence the locally inferred Hubble constant, potentially contributing to the $H_0$ tension, subject to stringent isotropy and dynamical consistency constraints. We identify observational strategies involving DESI, Rubin, peculiar velocity surveys, and cosmic void catalogues, opening a new avenue for testing whether the dark energy driving cosmic acceleration is truly homogeneous.

papers.title: Covariant Hamiltonian Gravity in Spherical Symmetry
papers.abstract: Building upon the covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, we construct the effective Einstein equation governing gravitational dynamics. For any prescribed one-parameter family of static, spherically symmetric metrics, this equation can be constructed such that the prescribed family constitutes their vacuum solutions. As an application, we construct generalized Vaidya solutions to the effective Einstein equation and show that the corresponding energy-momentum tensor takes precisely the standard Vaidya form. The results demonstrate that standard null dust sources can serve as matter source for dynamical black-hole geometries beyond general relativity, including regular black holes. Furthermore, this work suggests that quantum gravity corrections alone may not account for Hawking-like evaporation, as mass loss in the ingoing Vaidya solution necessarily requires a violation of the null energy condition within our effective framework.

papers.title: Probing faint radio activity from cores to filaments in two $z=2.24$ protoclusters with uGMRT
papers.abstract: We present deep 1.26 GHz radio continuum observations of the two $z=2.24$ protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) to investigate their members' radio emission and its possible environmental dependence. Among 187 and 105 H$\alpha$ emitter (HAE) members in BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, we identify ten and two robust radio counterparts, respectively, together with five potential counterparts from forced photometry. Two HAEs and the massive quiescent galaxy QG1 in BOSS1244 show strong radio excesses relative to their H$\alpha$-based star formation rates (SFRs) and are identified as strong radio-excess AGN candidates. Median stacking of the remaining 173 and 102 radio-undetected HAE members yields positive signals at $2.8\sigma$ and $3.2\sigma$ in BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, respectively. The stacked radio luminosities are consistent with those expected from the median H$\alpha$-based SFRs, indicating that star formation can account for the average faint radio emission. After excluding the robust radio counterparts, we divided the HAE members by the projected distance from QG1 in BOSS1244 and from the filament spine in BOSS1542. The largest stacked radio luminosities are found toward the denser regions in both systems, but the differences are not statistically significant, and stellar mass shows no significant dependence on environmental distance. These results identify strong radio-excess AGN candidates among the individually detected members, while the faint HAE population is on average consistent with radio emission from star formation. The similar environmental ordering is suggestive but remains tentative. Deeper radio observations at multiple frequencies and higher angular resolution are required to determine whether this apparent trend reflects weak AGN activity or variations in radio emission associated with star formation.

papers.title: Negative Dynamical Friction in Dark Matter Spikes around Rotating Black Holes
papers.abstract: Dark matter may affect extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) through orbital-energy exchange and a conservative metric response. Here we show that dark matter spikes around rotating massive black holes can drive negative dynamical friction, supplying orbital energy to secondary black holes on stable prograde circular orbits. The energy-gain region extends beyond the innermost stable circular orbit once the black-hole spin exceeds a model-dependent threshold. For an illustrative four-year inspiral with Milky Way--like halo parameters and mass ratio $q=10^{-5}$, the total dynamical-friction contribution produces a phase difference of order $10^2$ radians relative to vacuum. For the same system, the fixed-frequency environmental redshift correction is comparable in magnitude and opposite in sign to the first-order conservative self-force correction. Both environmental energy exchange and the conservative metric response are therefore essential to precision EMRI modeling.

papers.title: MeerKAT reveals an ultra-steep spectrum radio halo in Abell 370
papers.abstract: Hubble Frontier Field cluster Abell 370 ($z=0.375$) has been the target of a suite of legacy multi-wavelength observational campaigns and is a prime candidate to host a diffuse radio halo, given its high mass ($\sim10^{15}\,\rm{M_\odot}$) and non-relaxed dynamical state. Previous detections of its radio halo were of low significance and imaging fidelity, leading to an uncertain characterisation of its nature. We use deep MeerKAT Ultra-High Frequency observations ($580-1015\,\rm{MHz}$) to robustly map the halo's spatial extent and spectral properties. We find a radio emission size of $\sim 1.1\,\rm{Mpc}$, significantly larger than previously reported. We measure a MeerKAT UHF in-band integrated spectral index of $\alpha=-1.54\pm0.05$. This result is consistent with an ultra-steep spectrum radio halo ($\alpha\lesssim-1.5$). We find a strong, sub-linear correlation ($k=0.60\pm0.08$) between the radio and X-ray surface brightness. The radio halo's position on the $P_{1.4\,\rm{GHz}}-M_{500}$ scaling relation is underluminous, consistent with the known USSRH population. The combined evidence strongly supports that the diffuse central radio emission in Abell 370 is an Ultra-Steep Spectrum Radio Halo (USSRH), refining its previous classification and providing further support for the turbulent re-acceleration model.

papers.title: Pushing the accuracy of the quasi-circular baseline for the SEOBNR family of models
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations have opened a new era of astronomy, with accurate modeling of binary black hole signals becoming increasingly important for source characterization and astrophysical inference as detector sensitivities improve. We present SEOBNRv5iHM, an updated quasi-circular, aligned-spin inspiral-merger-ringdown gravitational-waveform model with higher-order modes, constructed within the effective-one-body formalism and building upon SEOBNRv5HM. The improvements mainly concern the late inspiral and the merger-ringdown: we remove the non-quasi-circular corrections used in previous models and instead introduce a phenomenological intermediate region between the inspiral and the ringdown, which allows the ringdown attachment time to be chosen independently for each mode, including at the peak of the mode's amplitude. The model is calibrated and validated against 591 quasi-circular aligned-spin waveforms from the third Simulating eXtreme Spacetimes catalog. For the $(2,2)$ mode, when considering the maximum unfaithfulness against numerical relativity over a total mass range of 10-300$M_\odot$, SEOBNRv5iHM achieves a median of $4.25\times10^{-5}$, a factor of 4.5 below SEOBNRv5HM, and a factor of 3-8 below other semi-analytical models, with $84\%$ of cases below $10^{-4}$. For $M\ge150 M_\odot$, the median drops to $9.7\times10^{-6}$, comparable to the numerical-relativity surrogate NRHybSur3dq8. For polarization mismatches at inclination $\pi/3$, with modes up to $\ell_\mathrm{max} = 5$, the median maximum unfaithfulness is $4.2\times10^{-4}$, a factor of 2.6 below SEOBNRv5HM, 1.9 below IMRPhenomTHM, and 6-11 below the other semi-analytical models. Since spin-precessing and eccentric models are built on top of the quasi-circular, aligned-spin baseline, these improvements will make future SEOBNR models more accurate, reducing waveform systematics in upcoming analyses.

papers.title: Smooth Rigidity Near Extremal Horizons
papers.abstract: The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section. The proof combines a terminal wave-map gauge with energy estimates on the orbit cylinder and yields a finite weighted matching criterion. For unwarped horizons with positive-Einstein sections, a condition on the full Lichnerowicz spectrum reduces the smooth classification to parallel first transverse data. All such data have convergent multiwarped Einstein realizations, including examples whose sections have negative sectional-curvature directions. We also obtain a finite-regularity version for round sections. The continuation argument extends to four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory and gives smooth charged-Nariai rigidity. Finally, rotating Nariai data admit the required spacelike graph throughout the regular branch; an all-order tensor estimate yields smooth Kerr--de Sitter or rotating-Nariai rigidity for $a^2/r_0^2\leq1/8$, without assuming ambient axial symmetry.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of a scale-dependent black hole in 5D spacetime with cosmological constant
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a scale-dependent black hole in five dimensions with a positive cosmological constant, considering i) scalar, ii) electromagnetic, and iii) Dirac perturbations. After deriving exact analytical solutions within the framework of scale-dependent gravity in five dimensions and selecting a different family of solutions (cf. \cite{Contreras:2019fwu}), we analyze the corresponding effective potentials (given by the lapse function) for each perturbation type. We employ a first-order approximation for the lapse function, as it closely matches the exact case for small $\varepsilon$. Since quantum corrections are expected to be small, our focus is on a relatively low range of the scale-dependent parameter $\varepsilon$. We confirm that the WKB semi-analytical approach can be used to compute the QNMs for these perturbations to the background geometry. We calculate the QNM frequencies for the classical case (for comparison) and for cases where the scale-dependent parameter $\varepsilon$, which quantifies deviations from General Relativity, is non-zero. The results are summarized in a series of tables and figures. Finally, we find that, regardless of the perturbation type, the solutions are stable, as the imaginary part of each QNM frequency is negative.

papers.title: Detecting Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from Galaxy Clusters: Distance Constraints
papers.abstract: We present a measurement of the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature using the largest galaxy cluster sample with spectroscopic redshift information to date, comprising 169,679 clusters selected from the WH24 catalogue based on the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. We measure the two-point correlation function in two redshift bins, $0.17\leq z<0.35$ and $0.35\leq z<0.5$, corresponding to effective redshifts of $z_{\rm eff}=0.25$ and $0.43$, with the BAO feature detected at approximately the $4\sigma$ level or above in both bins. By fitting the measured correlation functions, we obtain dilation parameters of $\alpha=0.97\pm0.07$ and $\alpha=1.01\pm0.04$, corresponding to volume-averaged distance measurements of $D_V/r_d=6.70\pm0.48$ and $D_V/r_d=11.25\pm0.47$, respectively. Using the Planck 2018 sound horizon calibration, we obtain $H_0=66.6 \pm 4.9 \,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ within the flat $\Lambda$CDM framework. We further combine our cluster BAO measurements with cosmic microwave background and Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova observations to constrain dynamical dark energy within the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder parametrization. The resulting constraints are consistent with $\Lambda$CDM, which lies within the $68\%$ joint credible region in the $w_0$--$w_a$ plane. Our results demonstrate the potential of galaxy clusters as complementary tracers for BAO measurements and cosmological constraints.

papers.title: Nonlinear Scalarization of Reissner-Nordström Black Holes in Scalar-Torsion-Maxwell Teleparallel Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear scalarization of Reissner-Nordström black holes in scalar-torsion-Maxwell teleparallel gravity, in which the scalar field is nonminimally coupled to the Weitzenböck invariant. We consider polynomial coupling functions that avoid tachyonic instabilities at the linear level, thereby exploring a scalarization mechanism driven by nonlinear effects. In the decoupling limit, we study the nonlinear evolution of finite-amplitude scalar perturbations and show that the inclusion of a sixth-order coupling term allows the scalar field to dynamically evolve toward nontrivial stationary configurations. This behavior can be understood in terms of the effective potential, which develops nontrivial local minima that provide a mechanism for nonlinear saturation. By numerically solving the fully coupled field equations, we construct asymptotically flat charged black hole solutions endowed with scalar hair. We classify these solutions according to the number of nodes in the scalar field profile, identifying multiple branches whose structure and multiplicity depend on the coupling parameters. We further show that the higher-order coupling progressively suppresses higher-node branches and characterize the scalar backreaction through deviations of the metric functions and the torsion scalar from the Reissner-Nordström background.

papers.title: Horizon-penetrating rotating black-hole configurations in VCDM
papers.abstract: A regular black-hole metric need not define a regular configuration of VCDM, whose preferred foliation is part of the gravitational solution. We construct stationary rotating, possibly charged configurations on the constant-auxiliary Einstein-Maxwell branch. Their Kerr-Newman and Kerr-Newman-de Sitter geometries carry nonzero constant-mean-curvature foliations that cross the future black-hole horizon and, in the de Sitter case, the future cosmological horizon. A horizon-regular flux formulation specifies the inner data and the distinct hyperboloidal and expanding asymptotic ends. Seventeen survey configurations are supplemented by a mean-flux scan at fixed four-geometry and paired flat/de Sitter comparisons down to $\kappa M = 0.01$, where $K_0 = 3\kappa$. Varying the flux changes the preferred-foliation shear without changing the background seen by standard test matter. The paired local lapse and shear differences have effective powers close to two over the computed range, with the lapse comparison requiring a fixed time normalization. Continuous residuals, geometric reconstructions, and selected grid comparisons test the numerical solutions. An exact lapse bound excludes zeros in the regular stationary exterior block with $\Delta_r > 0$. We distinguish singular finite-proper-distance endpoints from asymptotic trumpet ends and give conditional bounds on a stationary spacelike inner limit. A local cosmological interpretation requires additional matching assumptions; dynamical selection and the rotating interior endpoint are not determined by the stationary construction.

papers.title: Vacuum energy interacting with dark matter and dark radiation: alleviating the $H_0$-$S_8$ seesaw
papers.abstract: Extensions of $\Lambda$CDM that raise $H_0$ with additional energy before recombination, such as dark radiation and early dark energy (EDE), also raise $S_8$. We study whether a late-time energy exchange between the vacuum and the dark sector can offset this increase. The coupling rate scales as $\bar m H^{\alpha}$ and is negligible before recombination for $\alpha \le -2$; the energy is transferred along the four-velocity of geodesic cold dark matter, so the dark matter produced by the vacuum carries no density perturbation and slows the growth of structure. We add the exchange to dark radiation ($\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM) and to a one-parameter EDE model ($\bar m$EDE), and constrain the models with Planck 2018, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ data (CBS), and with the SH0ES calibration added (CBSH) to test the exchange when $H_0$ is held at a high value. For CBS the posteriors favour an energy flow from the vacuum into dark matter at 1.8-2.7$\sigma$, and the exchange lowers $S_8$ by 0.02-0.08 but does not raise $H_0$: $\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM gives $H_0 = 68.83 \pm 0.91$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, 3.1$\sigma$ below SH0ES. For CBSH the exchange removes the increase of $S_8$ caused by dark radiation, giving $S_8 = 0.800 \pm 0.016$ at $H_0 = 71.34 \pm 0.70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, and about a third of that caused by EDE for $\alpha = -2$, with the coupling at 1.1-2.0$\sigma$. The reduction of $S_8$ is concentrated at $z \lesssim 0.3$: at the redshifts probed by KiDS-Legacy the lensing amplitude decreases by only 1-2%, the shear $\chi^2$ of the dark-radiation models changes by less than 3, and the exchange reduces but does not remove the excess shear $\chi^2$ of EDE. A late-time exchange can therefore offset part of the $S_8$ increase of early-time solutions, but it does not ease the Hubble tension, and current data do not require it.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes of Black holes in the generalized Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution of $f(R)$ gravity
papers.abstract: We analyze scalar, vector, and {axial} tensor perturbations in a Schwarzschild-type static spherically symmetric solution of modified $f(R)$ gravity. A similar effect arises for the parameter $\eta$ when $A$ is small, while for larger $A$ values the effects are opposite, where the scalar perturbations display a distinct deviation compared to the vector and {axial} tensor cases. Contour plots of QNMs in the parameter space support these findings. Finally, time-domain profiles are obtained to illustrate the dynamical evolution of the gravitational wave signal.

papers.title: Efficiency enhancement in the Unruh quantum Otto engine
papers.abstract: We investigate the efficiency enhancement of an Unruh quantum Otto engine (UQOE) composed of two initially unentangled Unruh-DeWitt (UDW) detectors. The two detectors have different accelerations and interact with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We choose a diagonal free Hamiltonian for the UQOE and define its work and heat with respect to the proper time of one of the detectors. Consequently, the coherence terms generated through the interaction with the scalar field do not directly contribute to the work and heat of the UQOE. Instead, the efficiency enhancement arises from the relative proper-time factor, which assigns different weights to the population changes of the two detectors. We then identify cyclic operating points that satisfy the conditions of initial-state passivity, cycle closure, and energy conservation. Their efficiency is higher than that of a conventional UQOE, and the state of the UQOE after the heat-absorption stage is separable. Finally, we study the effect of the separation between the two detectors on the engine efficiency. During the interaction of the two detectors with the field, increasing their separation reduces the generated entanglement; however, this separation enters the nonlocal coherence terms, thereby restricting the range of parameter settings compatible with cycle closure and influencing the achievable efficiency enhancement. Our results demonstrate that the UQOE can achieve enhanced efficiency even when its state after the heat-absorption stroke is separable, showing that entanglement generation is not a necessary condition for efficiency enhancement.

papers.title: Single and repetitive Penrose processes in genuine uncharged Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson black hole

Finally, for repetitive extraction processes within the surveyed regime, all sequences terminate due to orbital accessibility obstructions, explicitly local-slope failure and far-field incident-branch closure, with the final black-hole state retaining most of its initial rotational energy reservoir. papers.title: Could globular clusters in the vicinity of the galactic centre have contributed stars to the nuclear star cluster in the past?
papers.abstract: The results of direct N-body simulations of three Milky Way bulge globular clusters - Terzan 2, Terzan 4, and Terzan 5 - evolving in a time-varying galactic potential derived from the IllustrisTNG-100 cosmological database over 8 Gyr are presented. To parametrize the effect of dynamical friction in the dense central environment, we introduce a velocity reduction factor (Vred) ranging from 1.00 to 0.10. The mass distribution of accreted stars reveals a bimodal structure: a low-mass component below 1 Msol whose capture is independent of Vred, and a prominent high-mass tail extending to 20 Msol corresponding to neutron stars and black holes, which grows with decreasing Vred. Notably, Terzan 4 is the only cluster for which white dwarfs are also captured by the NSC at every Vred value. Our results suggest that the Terzan family represents a more significant source of compact remnants for the Galactic NSC than previously studied clusters, while confirming that tidal stripping of surviving globular clusters alone cannot account for the total NSC mass.

papers.title: Deviations from Kerr: Critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters for general observer inclinations
papers.abstract: We study critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with separable null geodesics and Kerr angular structure. A Kerr-relative decomposition of the radial metric functions gives analytic first-order departures of these observables for observers at general inclination. Applications to representative metrics illustrate how different radial deformations produce distinct departures from Kerr around the critical curve. Comparisons with exact finite-deformation profiles and independent numerical calculations verify the first-order predictions on regular, accessible exterior photon-shell branches.

papers.title: Next-to-next-to-leading gravitational radiation-reaction corrections to quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic compact binary orbits
papers.abstract: We apply the Lagrange method of variation of constants to compute the radiation-reaction (RR) corrections to the quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic motion of compact binary systems at 4.5PN order, i.e., at next-to-next-to-leading order in the RR. We rely on the recent determination of the 4.5PN RR acceleration, in a general frame and in the center-of-mass frame, in harmonic coordinates. The non-local effects, due to the tails at 4PN order and to the gravitational-wave recoil at 4.5PN order, are carefully evaluated. Although the calculation is implemented differently in the quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic cases (different perturbation equations and choices of orbital parameters), we verify by analytic continuation that the results for the local effects are equivalent in the two cases.
